prompt:
Find real, documented examples of open-source maintainers publicly reporting AI-generated bug reports or pull requests as a burden (e.g. curl, Python, other projects). Cite the original posts and quote what they said.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

If you're not sure about something, just say so.

response.content:
Here are documented examples of open-source maintainers publicly reporting AI-generated bug reports as a burden, based on the provided search results. 

**curl project (Daniel Stenberg):**
Daniel Stenberg, the founder and lead of the curl project, has been very vocal about the drain on maintainers' time caused by AI-generated "slop" vulnerability reports. He notes that the volume of these reports acts as a DDoS attack on the project's limited security team, consuming hours of their time for zero valid results. He implemented an AI disclosure checkbox on HackerOne and started banning reporters who submit AI slop.

SOURCE: https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2025/07/14/death-by-a-thousand-slops/ | QUOTE: "Every report thus engages 3-4 persons. Perhaps for 30 minutes, sometimes up to an hour or three. Each." | CLAIM: AI slop vulnerability reports place a massive time burden on the curl security team.
SOURCE: https://daniel.haxx.se/blog/2025/07/14/death-by-a-thousand-slops/ | QUOTE: "In early July, about 5% of the submissions in 2025 had turned out to be genuine vulnerabilities. The valid-rate has decreased significantly compared to previous years." | CLAIM: The validity rate of bug reports has plummeted as the volume of AI slop has increased.
SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes_action_against_time-wasting_ai_bug_reports/267311 | QUOTE: "A threshold has been reached. We are effectively being DDoSed. If we could, we would charge them for this waste of our time." | CLAIM: Daniel Stenberg considers the flood of low-effort AI bug reports to be a DDoS-level burden on maintainers' time.
SOURCE: https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2025/05/open-source-project-curl-is-sick-of-users-submitting-ai-slop-vulnerabilities/ | QUOTE: "We still have not seen a single valid security report done with AI help" | CLAIM: Not a single AI-generated security report submitted to the curl project has turned out to be a genuine vulnerability.

**Python project (Seth Larson):**
Seth Larson, a maintainer for the Python project, has also spoken out about the cost of AI-generated security reports. He points out that because these reports appear legitimate on the surface, they require time-consuming investigation by trained specialists, which leads to maintainer burnout.

SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "Security reports that waste maintainers' time result in confusion, stress, frustration, and to top it off, a sense of isolation due to the secretive nature of security reports" | CLAIM: AI-generated bug reports cause severe emotional and psychological stress for open-source maintainers.
SOURCE: https://www.theregister.com/security/2025/05/07/curl-takes-action-against-time-wasting-ai-bug-reports/267311 | QUOTE: "responding to them is expensive and time-consuming because on face value, they seem legitimate and must be investigated further by trained eyes before confirming that they are, in fact, bogus." | CLAIM: AI bug reports drain maintainer resources because their plausible formatting forces manual verification.

**Other projects:**
While the provided search results mention that other projects are experiencing the same issue, they do not name specific maintainers or projects other than curl and Python, nor do they provide quotes from them.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Documented examples or quotes from maintainers of open-source projects other than curl and Python publicly reporting AI-generated bug reports as a burden.
